brief: A fictional coordinator prepares a weekend community workshop. They need to check which shared tools are available, reserve a short setup window, and leave clear handoff notes. They have about fifteen minutes between other tasks, prefer a compact checklist, and currently use a paper board. They may keep that workflow if a new product requires extensive setup.

They work from a shared tablet in brief sessions, need readable controls, and currently use a shared document with dated notes. They may defer a new tool when the immediate task is already clear.

brief: A fictional board-game club organizer coordinates recurring evening sessions. They need to compare room availability, track which games are requested, and post a concise plan. Their schedule changes during the week, they dislike repeated data entry, and currently use a group message thread. They may try a product when it makes an immediate coordination task easier, or return to the thread when others need a quick answer.
